issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וְדֹרֵךְ עֲנָבִים בְּמֹשֵׁךְ הַזָּרַע' means 'and the treader of grapes [will overtake] the one who draws/sows the seed' (i.e., the grape-treader overtakes the sower). The Chinese renders 'בְּמֹשֵׁךְ הַזָּרַע' as '那帶領後裔前來的' ('the one who leads descendants to come'), which misinterprets 'מֹשֵׁךְ' (drawing/pulling, i.e., sowing seed) and 'הַזָּרַע' (the seed) as 'leading descendants' — a substantive change in meaning. The correct sense is the sower of seed, not a leader of offspring.

The Hebrew 'תִּתְמוֹגַגְנָה' means 'will melt/flow' (from מוּג, to melt, dissolve, flow). The Chinese '都必流淌' ('will all flow') is acceptable for 'flow,' but the Hebrew also implies melting/dissolving; however, this is a minor nuance and not a clear error. The main issue is the previous clause.
